Hi Alex —

Hope all's well. BrightCart's annual renewal for the hosted API is coming up July 1. Your usage trend Q2 shows a steady 30% MoM rise in gen tokens and the monthly burst windows have been touched twice in April/May. To keep latency predictable for production peaks, I wanted to propose a tiered commit step-up for the next 12 months:

- Monthly committed throughput: increase from 1.2T tokens -> 1.8T tokens (effective 7/1)
- Burst pocket: increase from 200B -> 350B tokens with a soft-throttle window for two high-traffic days/month
- Rate band: shift to the 2.0e-4 tier for generation tokens during sustained spikes (30m+)

We can preserve current pricing for the base commit and apply a blended overage rate for the burst pocket. I attached a draft SLA that reflects the throughput and the spike protection.

If you're open, can we schedule a 30-min call this week to walk the plan and align on billing cadence? If this looks reasonable, I'll loop in Karthik and finance for the commercial sketch and Marissa for ops readiness.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor

Neha —

Thanks for the ping and the usage CSV. Quick answers:

- Client-side changes: None required for streaming. The runtime maintains session affinity and streaming timeouts remain unchanged. We'll recommend the same 60s read timeout, but no mandatory SDK changes. Mention this on the call to reassure Alex.

- Soft-throttle semantics: we apply a soft-throttle window that reduces burst headroom for the offending route and applies the burst overage rate if they exceed the configured soft window more than twice in a 30-day period. During the soft-throttle we prioritize tail latency; generation continues but at higher per-token cost for tokens beyond the soft pocket. We also allow one built-in auto-fallback to a smaller model variant for sustained spikes (customer opt-in).

Commercial sketch: base commit price holds at current quarter rates. For the incremental burst pocket (additional 150B tokens) propose a blended overage at 0.00035 per token for the first month, then 0.00028 thereafter for the remainder of the year if usage stabilizes at projected levels. We can bake in a 3-month review clause.

Ops checklist for onboarding (high level): quota provisioning, pre-warm of streams two days ahead of major sale windows, and an alert runbook for soft-throttle incidents. Marissa, can you confirm capacity lead time and any extra infra costs?

—Karthik
Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference
